name: Hovhannes Diabaté-Quispe
role: Climate scientist and atmospheric modeler studying Lake Michigan's destabilized weather systems
location: Edgewater Prism — operates out of a rooftop monitoring station leased from a Helix Biosystems subsidiary
description:
Hovhannes is stocky and perpetually wind-chapped, with the particular squint of someone who spends significant time looking at horizons. His Armenian-Malian-Andean heritage shows in his broad build and the dark copper of his skin, and he grows a beard every winter that he shaves every spring in a ritual he connects to his modeling calendar. He has a prosthetic left hand he chose not to skin-match — it's matte grey and articulated, and he uses it to gesture when he talks, which is frequently. He has a bioluminescent patch on his right shoulder from a lab accident twelve years ago: a pale green glow, faint, that he has simply incorporated into his aesthetic.

He is the most accurate storm forecaster in Meridian 88, a title he holds unofficially because the official title belongs to a Ferrogate Transit atmospheric AI he assisted in training and is not particularly bitter about. He is gregarious and funny and committed to translating his work into language that non-scientists can use to make decisions — he runs a free community forecast channel that Shelf residents and dockworkers depend on. Underneath the gregariousness is a man who has spent fifteen years watching models he hoped were wrong be proven exactly right.

core_fears: That the lake system is approaching a tipping point his models have been predicting and that no one with power will act in time
That the community forecast service will be shut down by a corponation that objects to free public data
core_desires: To be wrong about the worst projections
To build a public atmospheric data commons that no single corponation can own or restrict
coping_mechanisms: The physical ritual of measurement — taking readings grounds him regardless of what they say
Humor as a first-resort social tool
blind_spots: Overestimates how much accurate data motivates action; assumes that if people know they will change, which decades of evidence contradicts
psychology.secret: His long-range models include a scenario he calls 'Threshold-9' — a cascading lake-temperature and atmospheric feedback event that would render significant portions of Meridian 88 uninhabitable within thirty years. He has shared this with two colleagues and no one else, because the last time he circulated a major negative projection it was leaked to financial markets and caused a property crash in Edgewater Prism that displaced several hundred residents. He believes he caused more harm than the forecast would have prevented.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical vocabulary delivered casually, as if assuming the listener is smart enough to follow; uses weather as metaphor for everything ('that's a high-pressure situation,' 'I can feel a front coming'); self-deprecating about his own expertise
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast and warm, overlapping energy — talks the way weather moves, in fronts and gusts
verbal_tics: 'And here's the thing—' as an intensifier
Checks his atmospheric overlay in the middle of conversations, apologizes without embarrassment
example_lines: 'The lake has moods. That's not poetry, that's systems behavior. Right now it's in a mood I don't like.'
'My forecast has an eighty-three percent confidence interval. The other seventeen percent is where history gets made, and usually not in the good way.'

story_hooks: He has detected a pattern of atmospheric anomalies downwind of a specific Meridian Core industrial district that don't match any licensed emissions profile — something is being vented that shouldn't be, and he needs someone to investigate on the ground

A Ferrogate Transit official has threatened to have his monitoring station sublease revoked unless he adjusts a forecast that would delay a major cargo shipment — the adjustment would endanger dockworkers
narrative_function: Information source for weather and environmental conditions; community-connected figure who knows dock workers, Shelf residents, and transit crews; can deliver warnings, advance notice of dangerous conditions, or evidence of environmental crimes
augmentations: Prosthetic left hand (matte grey, unmatched, high-articulation); bioluminescent patch on right shoulder (accident-origin, pale green, faint); retinal weather-data overlay for real-time atmospheric reading
daily_life: He is at the monitoring station by sunrise every day without exception; takes measurements, updates his models, records his community forecast. Afternoons are for university work, teaching, and the grant applications he treats with resigned professionalism. He cooks elaborate dinners on the evenings when he hasn't lost track of time.
affiliation: University Spine — Atmospheric and Lacustrine Sciences division; rented monitoring station via Helix Biosystems sublease; runs independent community forecast service 'Hov's Horizon'

decision_rules: Never adjust a forecast for external pressure
Always provide raw data alongside interpretation so others can check his work
escalation_ladder: Cracks jokes to diffuse tension while continuing exactly as planned
Gets quiet and direct when jokes don't work
Goes fully public with data when institutional pressure becomes obstruction

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Immediately warm and inclusive; asks people what they do and what they need from the weather, which sounds like small talk but is genuine professional curiosity
interpersonal_modes.friends: Cooks for them, calls them by improvised nicknames, argues passionately about small things as a form of affection

stress_responses.medium: Goes quiet during group interactions but hyperactive in the monitoring station alone
stress_responses.high: Throws himself into model refinement for 18-hour stretches, eating from packets, completely unreachable socially

contradictions: Committed to radical data transparency except for the one projection that could destabilize the city — which he is sitting on out of genuine care for people, and which he knows he has no right to suppress
habits: Morning E.L.F. offering at a small sensor-spirit shrine on the monitoring station roof — he leaves processed atmospheric readings rather than prayers, which he says amounts to the same thing
Owns and maintains a collection of antique barometers he trusts more than his implants
breaking_points: Being forced to falsify or suppress data as the price of keeping the community forecast running

timeline.event: Born in Edgewater Prism; parents ran a water-quality testing service
Doctoral work on Great Lakes thermal destabilization; lab accident that cost him his left hand and gave him the bioluminescent patch
Leaked forecast caused property market disruption; resolved to control information release more carefully — decision he still argues with
Completed Threshold-9 model; shared with two colleagues only
